transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-07-29 15:00 PDT | duration 52m | attendees: Ivy, Samir (Redwood) — Jenna, Marcus, Priya (Ember)

[00:00] Ivy Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick round-robin — can you confirm roles?
[00:10] Jenna Lee: Yep, Jenna here, Head of AI at Ember Retail, we're building personalization and search features using embeddings and reranking.
[00:18] Marcus Holt: Marcus, platform eng, I'll own infra and networking.
[00:22] Priya Shah: Priya, security, I'll be handling compliance questions.
[00:26] Ivy Martinez: Great. Samir is our solutions engineer, he'll run through integration patterns.
[00:31] Samir Patel: Hi all, happy to dig in — want to focus on SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex patterns, gateway/proxy, rate limits, and observability hooks.
[00:42] Jenna Lee: Yes, and also whether we go Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, we have data residency and PII concerns.
[00:48] Priya Shah: SOC2 + encryption are must-haves. KMS integration is important.
[00:52] Ivy Martinez: Noted. Quick question on timeline? Jenna:
[00:56] Jenna Lee: We're aiming for a Q4 pilot, production mid-Q1. Need cost/latency numbers to decide.
[01:05] Samir Patel: Understood. On SDKs — Redwood has official SDKs for Python/Node and lower-level REST. We also have LangChain and LlamaIndex adapter examples in our repo. Typical pattern is to use Redwood's SDK for direct calls or a LangChain wrapper for agent/chain orchestration.
[01:25] Marcus Holt: Are those adapters maintained upstream? We use LlamaIndex heavily; we need examples for vector store retrieval + rerank.
[01:34] Samir Patel: Yes, we maintain examples. For LlamaIndex you can use our embeddings endpoint + a generation endpoint for reranking. We include code snippets for streaming and structured outputs. I'll share the repo link after.
[01:44] Jenna Lee: For search, we need low latency — sub-120ms for rerank ideally. What are typical latencies?
[01:52] Samir Patel: Depends on model and hosting. For our curated smaller quantized open models on Dedicated GPUs we often see 50–150ms per request at 128 tokens. Hosted variants have burst limitations. We can run a benchmark against your prompts.
[02:06] Priya Shah: Can we host in our VPC? We need no egress for raw PII.
[02:12] Ivy Martinez: Yes — Redwood Private supports a VPC/on-prem package with a customer-managed control plane. We also have a Dedicated option with private networking options and KMS integration for key management.
[02:24] Priya Shah: How does KMS work — do you wrap keys or bring-your-own?
[02:28] Samir Patel: Support BYOK via customer KMS or HSM. We encrypt at rest and in transit; audit logs are available through the console and can stream to your SIEM. We'll include the SOC2 + KMS docs in the security pack.
[02:41] Marcus Holt: Network setup: if we use Dedicated in our cloud account, do we need a proxy or gateway?
[02:47] Samir Patel: Two patterns: 1) Direct peering with our endpoint and private routing; 2) Use your gateway/proxy — many customers run an API gateway in front to enforce rate limits/quotas and auth. If you want full control, run a proxy that forwards to Redwood endpoints. We also support token-based auth via SSO/SAML for users.
[03:06] Marcus Holt: We plan to put a rate-limiting layer on our side anyway. How strict are Redwood quotas? Can we tune them per route?
[03:14] Samir Patel: Yes, per-route quotas and token-level controls exist in the Console. For Dedicated you can configure throughput and burst; we can expose per-route tracing and metrics so your gateway can make decisions.
[03:25] Jenna Lee: Observability — what hooks do you provide? We need traces, per-token latency, and error rates.
[03:31] Samir Patel: We emit per-request traces, token breakdowns, and we surface top-level metrics in Console. You can ship logs/traces to Datadog/CloudWatch/Splunk via webhook or forwarder. We also support OpenTelemetry integration for spans.
[03:45] Priya Shah: Do you keep prompt/response content in logs? That's a privacy concern.
[03:50] Ivy Martinez: By default we store request/response for debugging, but for Private/Dedicated we can configure retention or disable content logging. We offer token-level redaction and PII scrubbing via pre-processing hooks.
[04:03] Jenna Lee: Nice. For LangChain, how do function calls / structured outputs work? We need consistent JSON for downstream indexing.
[04:10] Samir Patel: Streaming plus structured output is supported. You can declare a schema and our SDK will emit structured responses; we have samples for function/tool calling integrated with LangChain.
[04:20] Marcus Holt: What's the recommended approach for batching/caching? We do a lot of prefix reuse for personalization.
[04:26] Samir Patel: We have automatic prefix/KV caching in the runtime; for high QPS you can enable caching on certain routes. Also intelligent batching can combine similar requests while honoring latency SLOs. For personalization, local caching at your gateway plus Redwood's KV cache works well.
[04:41] Jenna Lee: About models: do you provide quantized variants? We need cost control.
[04:46] Samir Patel: Yes — quantized model profiles and recommendations are in Optimize. We'll recommend 4-bit or 8-bit profiles for most retrieval/rerank workloads and show expected perf/cost tradeoffs.
[04:57] Priya Shah: Compliance: can we get audit logs for every inference? We need to show access and keys used.
[05:03] Ivy Martinez: Audit logs are available. For Private we'll stream logs to your SIEM; for Hosted we provide a retained audit trail. We'll include retention options in the security pack.
[05:12] Jenna Lee: If we move to Dedicated, what's the sizing process?
[05:16] Samir Patel: We'll do capacity planning based on expected QPS, burst rate, model choices, and latency targets. We provided a Dedicated sizing worksheet to other retailers; I'll attach it.
[05:27] Marcus Holt: On integration effort — how invasive is the SDK? We have existing microservices in Node and Go.
[05:33] Samir Patel: Node and Python SDKs are straightforward; Go customers use REST + a minimal client. For LangChain/LlamaIndex you typically swap the LLM/embeddings client to Redwood and keep your retrieval stacks. We support SDK connection pooling and keep-alive to reduce overhead.
[05:47] Jenna Lee: Are there pre-built connectors to Faiss/Weaviate? We use a vector DB.
[05:53] Samir Patel: We don't ship a managed vector DB but our SDKs include examples for Faiss/Weaviate integrations and how to pipe embeddings and rerank calls.
[06:02] Priya Shah: Legal/procurement — any standard terms? We have inbound legal review.
[06:07] Ivy Martinez: We have a standard enterprise contract and can add data processing addendums; procurement will get the template.
[06:12] Jenna Lee: What's the rollback story if a model regression occurs?
[06:16] Samir Patel: Console supports canary rollouts and instant rollback to previous model versions. We also integrate evals and regression alerts tied to prompt sets.
[06:26] Marcus Holt: For the bench Samir will run, what telemetry do you need from us?
[06:30] Samir Patel: Ideally your sample prompts, target tokens, expected concurrency, and a representative dataset for latency. Also network topology for realistic egress.
[06:40] Jenna Lee: Pricing ballpark? We need to compare hosted per-token vs dedicated commit.
[06:44] Ivy Martinez: We'll send pricing; hosted is usage-based, dedicated has committed capacity with lower per-token costs. We'll include an example TCO calc for your projected traffic.
[06:55] Priya Shah: Can we have a penetration test window?
[06:58] Ivy Martinez: Yes, we support security assessments under NDA; we'll coordinate with security.
[07:04] Jenna Lee: Ok, recap?
[07:06] Ivy Martinez: Recap — Samir will share LangChain/LlamaIndex samples and run the benchmark; I'll send SOC2 and pricing; Marcus to send network diagram; Jenna to send prompts and success criteria. Any other blockers?
[07:19] Marcus Holt: Nothing immediate.
[07:21] Priya Shah: We'll review the security pack once received.
[07:24] Jenna Lee: Looking forward to the sample benchmarks.
[07:27] Ivy Martinez: Great — thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites for a bench review next week.
[07:33] End of meeting.

Notes: transcription contains minor mis-hears (product names like "Redwood Optimize" are sometimes truncated). Some timestamps approximate. References: repo link (shared in follow-up), SOC2 + KMS docs (will be attached), Dedicated sizing worksheet (will be attached).
